Class AnnotationConversionUtils

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.core.annotation.AnnotationConversionUtils
@Internal public final class AnnotationConversionUtils extends Object
The conversions of a raw value to a basic type: a string, a number, a boolean or a character.

Each method checks for the form the value most likely has and returns it directly, and only otherwise delegates to the ConversionService. The methods that return an object answer null for a null value; the ones that return a primitive answer zero or false.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

      public static <E extends Enum<E>> @Nullable E toEnum(@Nullable Object value, E[] constants)
      Converts a value to an enum constant, by name: a constant is read by its name, and so is a string. The constants are the ones of the enum type, which the generated code supplies, so that nothing is looked up reflectively.
      Type Parameters:
      E - The enum type
      Parameters:
      value - The value, a constant or its name
      constants - The constants of the enum type
      Returns:
      The constant, null for null
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - When the enum type has no constant of that name

    • toAnnotation

      public static <T extends Annotation> @Nullable T toAnnotation(@Nullable Object value, Class<T> type, @Nullable AnnotationBuilder<T> builder, ConversionService conversionService)
      Reads a nested annotation from an instance, an AnnotationValue or a map of its members, through the builder registered for its type, or the conversion service when there is none. With a builder, the annotation is always one the builder created, which is an AnnotationValueProvider.
      Type Parameters:
      T - The annotation type
      Parameters:
      value - The raw value
      type - The annotation type
      builder - The builder of the annotation type, from annotationBuilder(Class), null when there is none
      conversionService - The conversion service
      Returns:
      The annotation, null when absent
